questions.q: Which period status allows a journal to actually post and update a GL balance?
options: Future Enterable
Never Opened
Permanently Closed
Open
questions.explain: Only the Open status allows journals to post normally and update balances.

questions.q: What can happen in a Future Enterable period?
options: Journals post to GL balances immediately
Nothing at all can happen
Subledger transactions can be entered and distributed, but cannot post to GL yet
Only reversal journals can be created
questions.explain: Future Enterable lets subledgers enter and distribute transactions dated in that period, but GL posting waits until the period is Open.

questions.q: Can two accounting periods be Open at the same time?
options: No, General Ledger forces exactly one open period
Yes, it's common for the closing period and the new period to both be Open around month-end
Only if they belong to different ledgers
Only during year-end close
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion does not require closing one period before opening the next; overlap is common and normal around month-end.

questions.q: What is an adjustment period used for?
options: Recording audit and true-up entries separately, dated at the fiscal year-end
Entering transactions for a future fiscal year
Replacing the December period entirely
Storing budget balances only
questions.explain: An adjustment period (sometimes called period 13) is dated at the fiscal year-end and isolates audit/true-up entries from ordinary December activity.

questions.q: Once a period is Permanently Closed, what can be done to it?
options: It can be reopened by any user with GL access
It can only be reopened by an administrator, never a regular user
It cannot be reopened at all
It automatically reopens at year-end
questions.explain: Permanently Closed is a final state used once a period's audit is complete — it cannot be reopened, unlike an ordinary Closed period.
